title: What Restorative Justice Tech Is
definition: Restorative Justice Tech: tech supporting restorative processes.
description:
Restorative Justice Tech: tech supporting restorative processes. This is Future Governance & Society at its most ambitious — circle platforms research, tech logistics engineering and victim safety operations converging on a single goal: making tech hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Governance & Society will decide agreement tracking outcomes this century. Restorative Justice Tech is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working tech hulls, the larger circle platforms vision stalls, and with it, the tech logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Restorative Justice Tech in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

title: Real Research Today: Restorative Justice Tech
definition: Today's documented research behind Restorative Justice Tech.
description:
The road to Restorative Justice Tech is already being paved. Citizens' assemblies (Ireland, France, Belgium) show sortition-based deliberation shaping national policy. The Artemis Accords (30+ signatories) set norms for lunar and space governance.

Prospera (Honduras ZEDE) and charter-city projects test zone-based governance. Together these programs form the circle platforms foundation that Restorative Justice Tech will build on — the tech logistics results, the victim safety methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as tech logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Restorative Justice Tech
definition: Estimates Restorative Justice Tech readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Restorative Justice Tech components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a tech hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Restorative Justice Tech Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Restorative Justice Tech operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Restorative Justice Tech installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 99379 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where circle platforms monitoring, tech logistics redundancy, or victim safety maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Restorative Justice Tech Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Restorative Justice Tech: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Restorative Justice Tech — tech supporting restorative processes.

Phase 1 — Prove (circle platforms): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (tech logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (victim safety): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (agreement tracking): tech hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and justice-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
